content.title: About
content.content: Pork chop, no salt is a cut of meat from the pork loin, usually 2–3 cm thick, without added salt or seasonings. Chops are cooked on the grill, skillet, or oven and often served as a main dish. The meat is rich in protein and contains a moderate amount of fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pork is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide.
Chops are often marinated in dairy products to tenderize them.
Traditional cuisines in many countries cook chops with apple cider vinegar or wine.
Pork provides vitamin B12, essential for the nervous system.
No‑salt chops are suitable for low‑sodium diets.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Pork chops contain about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Pork is a source of thiamine, riboflavin, niacin, and vitamin B6, which are involved in energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The meat provides iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Chops without added salt are appropriate for people monitoring sodium intake.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: Pork contains monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that can support heart health when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Pork should be cooked to an internal temperature of 71 °C to avoid salmonella and trichinella infections.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Chops contain a moderate amount of saturated fat, so individuals with high cholesterol should limit intake.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rarely, some people may be allergic to pork.

items.title: Additives
items.content: When buying pre‑packaged no‑salt chops, check for hidden preservatives or flavor enhancers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chops can be pan‑seared, baked, or grilled. They are often served with vegetable sides, mashed potatoes, or yogurt‑based sauces. For tenderness, lightly pound the meat and marinate in herbs before cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh chops in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C for no more than 2‑3 days. Frozen chops keep up to 6 months at –18 °C. Before cooking, check for off‑odors or discoloration; discard if any are present.
